//catalog-growth-correction: CORRECTION (issue #674). Several notes below justify a budget bump with the claim that adding copy to the root next-intl catalog 'lands in the shared chunk and so costs every route about 1 kB'. That claim is wrong and should not be reused as precedent. It was first written in //media-picker, then cited by //multi-creator; //planner-serving-allocations rests on the same reasoning. Message catalogs do not contribute to First Load JS. Evidence: (1) a production build was searched for distinctive strings from three namespaces (mediaPicker, pwa, common) -- zero matches in .next/static/**/*.js, matches only in .next/server/chunks/*.js, because src/app/layout.tsx passes messages to NextIntlClientProvider as a prop, so they are serialized into the per-request RSC flight payload rather than compiled into a client chunk; (2) the / route is a clean control -- it renders no image field and no co-creator UI, and it has not moved (224.0 kB on a local Windows build) across both the mediaPicker and the recipeCreators catalog additions, though the claim predicts +1 kB for each. What actually moved those routes was code, not copy: the ~1 kB was ImageUploadField / media-picker-config wiring, which per-route module analysis found on exactly the three routes that grew and absent from /. The budget numbers below are NOT changed by this correction -- they were re-baselined to values that the measured routes genuinely need, so the limits are sound even though the stated reasoning was not. Only the diagnosis is corrected. The real cost of catalog growth is RSC payload transfer and hydration, which this gate does not measure at all; per-route message scoping is tracked in #674. Note the constraint any such change faces: use-intl's IntlProvider replaces messages on nesting rather than merging them, so a nested provider carrying only route namespaces would drop the globals. Before bumping a budget for 'catalog growth' again, measure which modules entered the route.

//multi-creator: SUPERSEDED -- see //catalog-growth-correction above. Measured after the fact (#668 session): #683 changed /recipes first-load JS by ZERO -- 253 kB on both sides of 45f9c79, with byte-identical shared-chunk hashes despite ~37 new catalog keys x 4 locales -- so the catalog mechanism cited below is ruled out by direct measurement as well as by the string search. Hash equality is the stronger form, because it also rules out compensating changes that a kB total would hide. The mid-branch Linux failure (254.0 vs 253) was real but TRANSIENT: the branch's final pre-merge run measured 253.0, which passes the original 253 budget under `actual <= budget` (check-bundle-budget.mjs:70). Note that is a claim about what would have turned CI red, not about actual bytes: next build prints First Load JS as integers at this magnitude, so the true size could be 253.4 and still print 253 -- but the gate only ever compares the printed number. So the 253 -> 255 bump was not load-bearing at merge -- BUT KEEP IT. /recipes still measures 253.0 on Linux, so reverting restores a zero-headroom budget, and zero headroom is the underlying fault this whole correction is about. RECONFIRMED (#819): Linux CI run 31449970781 reads /recipes at 253.0 against 255, 2.0 kB free -- this KEEP argument is still true on live CI, unlike the 307 figure below. No replacement cause is offered for the transient kB because none was established; do not substitute one. RECONCILED (#819): read that together with the byte-identical A/B earlier in this note, which is stronger than an open question -- it establishes there was no surviving kB to explain, so the abstention stands as a standing prohibition on substituting a guess, NOT as an admission that the cause is unknown and awaiting discovery. The general rule: decline to substitute a guess, but replace an abstention with a measurement as soon as one exists. Adding the measurement beside the abstention rather than in place of it leaves both standing, which reads as though the measurement settled nothing. Issue #668 adds the co-creator management and invitation copy to the root next-intl catalog, which lands in the shared chunk and so costs every route about 1 kB — the same pattern as //media-picker above. /recipes was already at exactly its 253 kB budget on main (zero headroom), so that kB tipped the Linux CI build to 254 and turned the gate red on a route this PR does not otherwise touch: no co-creator UI renders on /recipes. Its budget moves 253 -> 255 for a small honest margin (~0.8% headroom) rather than inflating any other route. The co-creator UI itself is confined to /recipes/[cook]/[recipe] (owner-only panel, 306 -> 307 against a 308 budget) and /notifications (untracked). REMEASURED (issue #819): that 307 is now STALE -- the route measures 308 on both platforms, 308.0 on a local Windows build and 308 on Linux CI (run 31449970781), against the 308 budget. It passes only because the gate compares actual <= budget, so headroom is zero and one displayed kB of growth turns main red. Concretely: tightening this budget to 306 OR TO 307 would be red today, and 307 is exactly the value the stale figure invites a reader to think is safe -- a planned 308 -> 306 tightening was already abandoned on the strength of it (#763). Re-measure before trusting any number in this file; a measurement recorded once and never re-taken decays into the guess it replaced. / and /recipes/[cook]/[recipe]/edit are unchanged; / remains at zero headroom and trimming the client message payload remains the intended follow-up.

//food-classifier-correction: CORRECTION (issue #821). The //-note above justifies the /recipes/[id] 280->290 bump for #558 with the claim that the reader's ingredients panel imports the food classifier (food-units -> food-db curated dataset) and that, because volumeClassForItem is a synchronous render-path helper, 'it can't be code-split and lands in first-load'. The first half is still true as source -- src/components/recipe/ingredients-panel.tsx:26 does statically import it into a 'use client' module -- but the conclusion does NOT hold today: removing the import entirely moves the route by ZERO. Measured on 41b6a583, local Windows build: /recipes/[cook]/[recipe] reads 308.0 kB both with the real import and with volumeClassForItem replaced by an inline constant, with the page's own chunk unchanged at 199 B. The control that makes that a true negative rather than a failed experiment: the string 'volumeClass' appears in 0 of the route's 33 first-load chunks in the stubbed build, so the referent was genuinely gone -- while 'buttermilk' still appears in 6 of them and 'sodiumMg' in 1. The curated food data therefore reaches this route by at least one further path that survives the removal, and no honest headroom can be bought by code-splitting the classifier. That further path is NOT identified here; do not substitute a guess for it (same standing prohibition as //multi-creator). What this does and does not settle: the 280->290 bump itself is NOT reverted -- the route genuinely measured ~286 at the time and measures 308 now, so the limit is sound; only the stated cause is corrected, and only as of this commit. The note may well have been accurate when written and been overtaken by a later import, which is the same 'true when made' decay //multi-creator documents. This is the third diagnosis in this file corrected by measurement (#674 catalogs, #820 stale figure, this one), and all three were reached by reasoning about which module 'must' be responsible rather than by removing it and rebuilding. Prefer that experiment: stub the suspected import, rebuild, and assert the identifier is absent from the route's chunks before believing the delta.
//headroom-requirement: Issue #796: a budget that is NEW or RAISED must leave at least 2 kB above the value the same run measures, or the gate fails and names the minimum acceptable number. Budgets you do not touch are never subject to this — inheriting an existing tight budget is not a failure, and three routes below sit at zero headroom for exactly that reason. Size a new budget from CI figures, not local ones: Linux reads about 1 kB above a local Windows build, and 'next build' prints whole kB, so a sub-kB webpack redistribution can move a route a full displayed kilobyte with no code change (measured at 145 bytes in #789). The 2 kB is the same band the NEAR warning uses, so a budget that passes this check is one the warning will stay quiet about. The check needs the base ref's copy of this file; when it cannot be read it SKIPS rather than fails.

//measured.//: Machine-checked measurement claims (#858). check-bundle-budget.mjs verifies each of these against the same build that enforces the budgets below, and FAILS when one no longer matches. The prose notes above explain reasoning; these entries are what CI holds to reality. Four claims in this file have been corrected after the fact -- #674/#690, #763, #820 and #857 -- each found by a person who happened to look, because nothing compared them to a build. A claim is only about the platform that produced it: Linux CI reads ~1 kB above a local Windows build, so entries for other platforms are skipped rather than failed, and an entry with no platform fails as malformed. Update the number and the runId together; a value you cannot re-derive is a value you cannot audit.
